title: Romans Chapter 16 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 16 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 16 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 16.

questions.question: In Romans 16, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus
Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us
Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen
questions.explanation: Phebe is commended at the very beginning of Romans 16, verse 1.

questions.question: Who is commended as a servant of the church at Cenchrea?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:1 states, 'I commend unto you Phebe our sister, which is a servant of the church which is at Cenchrea.'

questions.question: According to Romans 16, how should the recipients receive Phebe?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:2 instructs to receive her 'as becometh saints.'

questions.question: Who are described as Paul's helpers in Christ Jesus?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:3 says, 'Greet Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus.'

questions.question: What did Priscilla and Aquila do for Paul?
options: Laid down their own necks for his life
Laboured much on behalf of the church
questions.correctAnswer: Laid down their own necks for his life
questions.explanation: Romans 16:4 states they 'have for my life laid down their own necks.'

questions.question: Where was the church that meets in the house of Priscilla and Aquila located?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:5 says, 'Likewise greet the church that is in their house.'

questions.question: Who is called the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:5 mentions 'Salute my wellbeloved Epaenetus, who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ.'

questions.question: Who bestowed much labour on Paul and his companions?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:6 states, 'Greet Mary, who bestowed much labour on us.'

questions.question: Which two people are described as Paul's kinsmen and fellow prisoners?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:7 says, 'Salute Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen, and my fellowprisoners.'

questions.question: Who is called 'my beloved in the Lord' by Paul in Romans 16?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:8 states, 'Greet Amplias my beloved in the Lord.'

questions.question: Who are identified as helpers in Christ in Romans 16:9?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:9 says, 'Salute Urbane, our helper in Christ, and Stachys my beloved.'

questions.question: Phebe is described as a succourer of many and of Paul himself.
questions.explanation: Romans 16:2 states that Phebe 'hath been a succourer of many, and of myself also.'

questions.question: Priscilla and Aquila were thanked not only by Paul but also by all the churches of the Gentiles.
questions.explanation: Romans 16:4 says Paul gives thanks to them and 'also all the churches of the Gentiles.'

questions.question: Romans 16 states that Junia was a woman who was noted among the apostles.
questions.explanation: Romans 16:7 mentions Junia as being 'of note among the apostles,' but it does not explicitly state Junia was a woman.

questions.question: Romans 16 says that Mary was a servant of the church at Cenchrea.
questions.explanation: Romans 16:1 describes Phebe as a servant of the church at Cenchrea, but Mary is only said to have bestowed much labour on Paul and his companions (Romans 16:6).

medium.title: Romans Chapter 16 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 16 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who is referred to as 'approved in Christ' in Romans 16?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is Apelles, as stated in Romans 16:10: 'Salute Apelles approved in Christ.'

questions.question: What does Romans 16:11 promise will happen if someone greets those of Narcissus' household?
questions.explanation: While Romans 16:11 does not explicitly promise a blessing, the context of greeting fellow believers suggests a positive outcome of encouragement and fellowship.

questions.question: Who labored much in the Lord according to Romans 16:12?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:12 states: 'Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord.'

questions.question: What should believers do according to Romans 16:17?
options: Mark and avoid those causing divisions
Greet one another with a holy kiss
questions.correctAnswer: Mark and avoid those causing divisions
questions.explanation: Romans 16:17 advises believers to 'mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.'

questions.question: Which household is mentioned in Romans 16:10?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically mentions: 'Salute them which are of Aristobulus' household.'

questions.question: What does Romans 16:16 instruct believers to do?
options: Salute one another with an holy kiss
questions.correctAnswer: Salute one another with an holy kiss
questions.explanation: Romans 16:16 says: 'Salute one another with an holy kiss. The churches of Christ salute you.'

questions.question: What is said about Rufus in Romans 16:13?
options: He is chosen in the Lord
He is a helper in Christ
questions.correctAnswer: He is chosen in the Lord
questions.explanation: Romans 16:13 states: 'Salute Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.'

questions.question: What do those causing divisions serve according to Romans 16:18?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:18 states that 'they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.'

questions.question: According to Romans 16:14, who is mentioned alongside Asyncritus and Phlegon?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:14 lists: 'Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brethren which are with them.'

questions.question: In Romans 16:15, who is mentioned as part of the greeting?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions: 'Salute Philologus, and Julia, Nereus, and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints which are with them.'

questions.question: What does Romans 16:17 advise believers regarding those who cause offences?
questions.explanation: The instruction in Romans 16:17 is to 'avoid them' who cause divisions contrary to the doctrine.

questions.question: Who are mentioned as laborers in the Lord in Romans 16:12?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:12 highlights: 'Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labour in the Lord.'

questions.question: True or False: Romans 16:16 encourages believers to greet each other with a holy kiss.
questions.explanation: Romans 16:16 states: 'Salute one another with an holy kiss.'

questions.question: True or False: Romans 16:18 states that those who cause divisions serve our Lord Jesus Christ.
questions.explanation: Romans 16:18 clarifies that they serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 16:10 mentions Apelles as someone approved in Christ.
questions.explanation: Romans 16:10 specifically states: 'Salute Apelles approved in Christ.'

hard.title: Romans Chapter 16 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 16.

questions.question: What is Paul glad about concerning the Romans in Romans 16:19?
options: Their obedience is known to all men
questions.correctAnswer: Their obedience is known to all men
questions.explanation: Paul expresses his gladness about their obedience, stating that it has become known to all men (Romans 16:19).

questions.question: According to Romans 16:20, what will the God of peace do?
options: Bruise Satan under your feet shortly
questions.correctAnswer: Bruise Satan under your feet shortly
questions.explanation: The verse states that the God of peace will bruise Satan under their feet shortly, indicating a promise of victory over evil (Romans 16:20).

questions.question: Who is mentioned as a workfellow of Paul in Romans 16:21?
questions.explanation: Paul specifically mentions Timotheus as his workfellow in Romans 16:21.

questions.question: What does Tertius do in Romans 16:22?
questions.explanation: Tertius identifies himself as the one who wrote the epistle, greeting the recipients in the Lord (Romans 16:22).

questions.question: In Romans 16:25, who has the power to establish believers according to Paul's gospel?
questions.explanation: The verse states that it is the everlasting God who has the power to establish believers according to the gospel (Romans 16:25).

questions.question: What is the mystery mentioned in Romans 16:25 that has been revealed?
questions.explanation: The mystery now made manifest is that it is made known to all nations for the obedience of faith (Romans 16:26).

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'stablish' in Romans 16:25 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'stablish' refers to the act of confirming or strengthening someone in faith (Romans 16:25).

questions.question: Which literary technique is predominantly used in Romans 16:19 regarding good and evil?
questions.explanation: The contrast between being wise unto good and simple concerning evil illustrates the use of antithesis (Romans 16:19).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of obedience in Romans 16:19?
questions.explanation: James 1:22 encourages believers to be doers of the word, paralleling the emphasis on obedience in Romans 16:19.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of peace in Romans 16:20?
questions.explanation: Philippians 4:7 speaks of the peace of God which guards hearts, echoing the promise of peace in Romans 16:20.

questions.question: What precedes the statement in Romans 16:20 regarding the God of peace?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:17 precedes this statement, where Paul warns about those causing divisions (Romans 16:20).

questions.question: What does the mention of 'the churches of Christ' in Romans 16:16 imply about early Christian community?
questions.explanation: The salute from the churches of Christ suggests a sense of unity among the early Christian community (Romans 16:16).

questions.question: According to Romans 16:27, to whom is glory given?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that glory is given to God only wise through Jesus Christ (Romans 16:27).

questions.question: The statement 'The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all' appears in which verses?
questions.explanation: This statement appears in both Romans 16:24 and Romans 16:20, emphasizing grace's importance.

questions.question: Paul's mention of 'the firstfruits of Achaia' in Romans 16:5 suggests that he believed in the concept of predestination.
questions.explanation: The mention of the firstfruits indicates acknowledgment of early converts but does not directly imply a belief in predestination (Romans 16:5).

theological.title: Romans Chapter 16 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 16 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 16:17 teach about the nature of false teachers within the church?
options: They cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine learned
They are to be welcomed and taught patiently
They serve the Lord by correcting errors
They are examples of humility and repentance
questions.correctAnswer: They cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine learned
questions.explanation: Romans 16:17 explicitly states that believers are to mark and avoid those who cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine which was learned, emphasizing the danger of false teachers who disrupt church unity.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's revelation and the gospel is taught in Romans 16:25?
options: Christ's gospel is based on a mystery that was kept secret but now revealed
The gospel was fully understood and proclaimed from the beginning of the world
Christ's power is limited to the Jewish people only
The gospel is independent of revelation and mystery
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's gospel is based on a mystery that was kept secret but now revealed
questions.explanation: Romans 16:25 teaches that the gospel and preaching of Jesus Christ are according to the revelation of a mystery that was hidden since the world began but is now made manifest, highlighting the progressive unveiling of God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning Christian fellowship and mutual support is taught in Romans 16:2?
options: Believers are to receive and assist those who serve the church as befits saints
Christian service is optional and only for some gifted individuals
Church servants should be supported only by clergy
Mutual assistance is discouraged to maintain independence
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are to receive and assist those who serve the church as befits saints
questions.explanation: Romans 16:2 teaches that Phebe, a servant of the church, should be received in the Lord as is fitting for saints and assisted in whatever business she needs, emphasizing the doctrine of mutual support and honor within the body of Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 16:27 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:27 gives glory to God only wise through Jesus Christ forever, explicitly recognizing God's attribute of wisdom as central to the understanding of salvation and divine revelation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in Romans 16:20?
options: God's power to bring peace and defeat Satan
questions.correctAnswer: God's power to bring peace and defeat Satan
questions.explanation: Romans 16:20 declares that the God of peace will soon crush Satan under the believers' feet, demonstrating God's sovereign power over evil and His role as the bringer of peace.

questions.question: How does Romans 16:7 connect to the broader New Testament theme of apostolic authority and early church witness?
options: It affirms Andronicus and Junia as notable apostles predating Paul, underscoring apostolic legitimacy
It denies the authority of all apostles except Paul
It teaches that only Jewish leaders can be apostles
It suggests apostleship is purely honorary without real authority
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms Andronicus and Junia as notable apostles predating Paul, underscoring apostolic legitimacy
questions.explanation: Romans 16:7 recognizes Andronicus and Junia as 'of note among the apostles' and their prior faith in Christ, linking to the New Testament emphasis on apostolic authority as foundational for the church's teaching and witness.

questions.question: How does Romans 16:26 relate to Old Testament prophecy and the universal mission of the gospel?
options: It shows the gospel was revealed through prophets to all nations for obedience of faith
It limits the gospel to Israel alone
It states the gospel was a secret never to be revealed
It claims the gospel contradicts Old Testament prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the gospel was revealed through prophets to all nations for obedience of faith
questions.explanation: Romans 16:26 teaches that the mystery now revealed was made known by the scriptures of the prophets and the commandment of the everlasting God to all nations, emphasizing the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy about the Gentile mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 16:17 and Romans 16:18 teach about false teachers and their motives?
options: False teachers cause divisions and serve their own appetites, deceiving the simple
False teachers build up the church through humility
False teachers serve Christ by exposing errors in doctrine
False teachers are motivated by zeal for truth without error
questions.correctAnswer: False teachers cause divisions and serve their own appetites, deceiving the simple
questions.explanation: Romans 16:17 warns to mark and avoid those causing divisions contrary to doctrine; Romans 16:18 explains their motive is selfishness, not serving Christ, and they deceive with smooth words, revealing a doctrine about the corrupt nature of false teachers.

questions.question: What combined theological truth is taught by Romans 16:25 and Romans 16:26 regarding the mystery of the gospel?
options: The gospel mystery was hidden but revealed through prophetic scripture for universal obedience
The gospel was common knowledge from the world's foundation with no mystery
The gospel mystery is only for the Jewish people and remains secret to Gentiles
The gospel was revealed by human wisdom apart from prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel mystery was hidden but revealed through prophetic scripture for universal obedience
questions.explanation: Romans 16:25 speaks of a mystery kept secret until now, and 16:26 clarifies that this mystery is made manifest by the prophets' scriptures to all nations for obedience, together teaching the progressive revelation and universal scope of salvation.

questions.question: What theological synthesis can be drawn from Romans 16:1 and Romans 16:2 about the role and reception of women in early church ministry?
options: Women like Phebe served as deacons and were to be received and assisted as saints
Women were excluded from any church service or ministry roles
The early church discouraged support for women in ministry
Women only served in secular roles unrelated to the church
questions.correctAnswer: Women like Phebe served as deacons and were to be received and assisted as saints
questions.explanation: Romans 16:1 identifies Phebe as a servant (deacon) of the church, and 16:2 commands that she be received and helped as befits saints, indicating the recognized and honored role of women in ministry and the community's duty to support them.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Romans 16:7 promotes the idea that women cannot be apostles because Junia is a female name. What does Romans 16:7 actually teach?
options: Junia is noted among the apostles, implying female apostleship was recognized
Junia is never mentioned, so women apostleship is denied
Romans 16:7 only praises male apostles and excludes women
Junia was a man, so no female apostleship is implied
questions.correctAnswer: Junia is noted among the apostles, implying female apostleship was recognized
questions.explanation: Romans 16:7 explicitly refers to Junia alongside Andronicus as notable among the apostles, which indicates the early church recognized a female apostle named Junia, contrary to skeptical claims denying female apostleship.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of Christian unity and mutual affection is taught in Romans 16:16?
options: Believers are commanded to greet one another with a holy kiss, symbolizing unity and love
Believers should maintain distance and avoid physical greetings
Churches do not communicate or greet each other
Christian greetings are optional and culturally irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are commanded to greet one another with a holy kiss, symbolizing unity and love
questions.explanation: Romans 16:16 commands believers to salute one another with a holy kiss, a cultural expression of affectionate unity and love within the body of Christ, emphasizing the doctrine of mutual fellowship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Romans 16:24, the closing benediction of the chapter?
questions.explanation: Romans 16:24 closes with a blessing invoking the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, underscoring the divine attribute of grace as foundational to Christian life and salvation.

questions.question: How does Romans 16:19 relate to the theological tension between wisdom and simplicity in the Christian life?
options: Believers are to be wise concerning good but simple concerning evil
Believers should be wise about evil and simple about good
Christian life requires complexity in all matters
Believers should avoid wisdom and rely solely on emotion
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are to be wise concerning good but simple concerning evil
questions.explanation: Romans 16:19 exhorts believers to be wise to what is good and innocent (simple) concerning evil, teaching a doctrinal balance of spiritual discernment and moral purity in Christian conduct.

questions.question: What theological insight about spiritual suffering and partnership in Christ is found in Romans 16:7?
options: Andronicus and Junia were Paul's kinsmen and fellow prisoners, sharing in sufferings for Christ
Paul's associates avoided suffering and imprisonment
Spiritual suffering is optional and unrelated to apostleship
Fellow prisoners are excluded from apostolic honor
questions.correctAnswer: Andronicus and Junia were Paul's kinsmen and fellow prisoners, sharing in sufferings for Christ
questions.explanation: Romans 16:7 describes Andronicus and Junia as kinsmen and fellow prisoners who were notable among apostles, highlighting the doctrine that faithful Christian witness often involves suffering and partnership with Christ in trials.
